note: DRAFT ideological families. Vectors are illustrative starting points defined by the project team, not measurements of real people. Review with a diverse panel before launch. Persona names are about ideas only.

families.name: Restructuring Federalist

persona.name: The Jollof Federalist
persona.roast: Every state should cook its own pot, and you will defend the recipe at length.

families.description: Believes power and resources should move closer to states and regions, with a lighter centre and merit-based leadership.

families.name: Market Reformer

persona.name: The Owambe Capitalist
persona.roast: You think the economy is the party and the government should stop blocking the gate.

families.description: Trusts markets, private investment and open trade to create jobs, and wants the state to step back from business.

families.name: Social Democrat

persona.name: The Talakawa Champion
persona.roast: You believe the pot should feed everyone, and you have already counted the spoons.

families.description: Wants an active state that funds education, health and welfare, backed by strong democratic institutions.

families.name: Civic Nationalist

persona.name: The Green-White-Green Loyalist
persona.roast: Your first identity is Nigerian, and you will say so at every family meeting.

families.description: Puts a shared national identity first and prefers a strong, merit-based, secular public sphere.

families.name: Faith-Guided Traditionalist

persona.name: The Heirloom Keeper
persona.roast: You treat tradition like a family heirloom: polished, protected, and not for sale.

families.description: Wants faith and long-standing social norms to shape public life and law.

families.name: Regional Balancer

persona.name: The Balance Keeper
persona.roast: You would split the meat fairly across the whole village so nobody leaves the table angry.

families.description: Sees regional and ethnic balance, rotation and quotas as the price of a fair, stable federation.

families.name: Order-First Pragmatist

persona.name: The NEPA Realist
persona.roast: Make it work first. The debate can happen after the light comes.

families.description: Prioritises security, firm leadership and tough enforcement, even at some cost to openness.

families.name: Peacebuilder

persona.name: The Bus-Stop Peacemaker
persona.roast: You believe most fights end faster if everyone just sits down first.

families.description: Favours dialogue, rehabilitation and addressing root causes of conflict, with reform over punishment.

families.name: Economic Nationalist

persona.name: The Made-in-Naija Defender
persona.roast: If it can be made here, you want it made here, and you have opinions about the shortcut.

families.description: Wants to protect local producers and limit foreign control of key industries.

families.name: Youth Civic Reformer

persona.name: The Group-Chat Reformer
persona.roast: You could fix the whole system by Monday if someone would just add you to the committee.

families.description: Wants transparent, merit-based, rules-driven government, open to change and to the wider world.

families.name: Rule-of-Law Liberal

persona.name: The Constitution Carrier
persona.roast: You keep a copy of the constitution in your bag and you are not afraid to quote it.

families.description: Puts individual rights, independent courts and open debate first, with a modern, open outlook.

families.name: Welfare Nationalist

persona.name: The Subsidy Defender
persona.roast: Nobody should be left behind, and you will say so at the filling station.

families.description: Wants a strong national state that protects ordinary people from hard times and shields local producers.

families.name: Pan-African Integrationist

persona.name: The ECOWAS Passport Holder
persona.roast: Borders are lines on a map, and you have the stamps to prove it.

families.description: Believes Nigeria grows by opening up to its neighbours, Africa and the wider world.

families.name: Community Guardian

persona.name: The Village Square Elder
persona.roast: You trust the elders, the market square and a long conversation under the tree.

families.description: Prefers local solutions, community leadership, shared values and talking things through.

families.name: Technocratic Modernizer

persona.name: The Spreadsheet Patriot
persona.roast: You believe most of Nigeria's problems can be fixed with a good dashboard and a cleaner procurement process.

families.description: Trusts data, competence and better systems to deliver growth and cut corruption.

families.name: Faith-Led Social Reformer

persona.name: The Charity-Drive Captain
persona.roast: Faith is for feeding people, and you are already organising the truck.

families.description: Draws on faith to push for care for the poor, dialogue and community healing.

centrist_persona.name: The Fence Sitter
centrist_persona.roast: You see both sides so clearly that you are still waiting for the third one to show up.
centrist_persona.description: Your answers sit close to the middle on most axes, or they pull in different directions.
